key_insight: The paper shows that SFT difficulty is driven by a long-tail “prior barrier”: rare concepts start with weaker pretrained support and need more targeted supervision than frequent concepts.
engineering_relevance: For practical LLM fine-tuning, instruction data should be selected adaptively rather than uniformly so scarce concepts receive enough evidence under limited annotation budgets.
method: Defines prior barrier to measure how strongly pretrained concepts compete against the target concept
Analyzes long-tail prior barriers and derives a predictive risk bound linking barrier strength with accumulated SFT evidence
Introduces PASS, which selects instructions adaptively by estimating evidence coverage and prioritizing under-covered concepts
evidence_signal: The method is reported to outperform seven state-of-the-art instruction selection approaches across four backbone-budget settings, with ablations showing adaptive allocation beats uniform allocation.
watch_item: PASS depends on estimating concept-level evidence and coverage accurately, so performance may be sensitive to how reference-derived concepts are constructed and how well the selection proxy matches the downstream task.
paper_title: Overcoming Prior Barriers: Supervised Fine-Tuning under Long-Tail Distribution
